name: team_2015
caption:
IF OUR 2015 CHAMPIONSHIP STARTERS WERE POKÉMON 🎮🏀

🌊 Steph Curry = Lugia: one flutter of its wings can blow apart houses. First MVP season, 23.8 a night
💦 Klay Thompson = Squirtle: shoots water at its prey. The other Splash Brother, 43.9% from three
🛡️ Harrison Barnes = Corviknight: a steel body that terrifies any foe. 82 games, 82 starts
🦞 Draymond Green = Crawdaunt: a brute that loves to battle. 8.2 rebounds and 3.7 assists a night
🦎 Andre Iguodala = Kecleon: blends in, then strikes unnoticed. 0 starts all season, then Finals MVP

That's a team we're taking into any gym in the league. Who would you change? 👇

Even a light flutter of its wings can blow apart houses.

beats.vo: Built like steel. Eighty-two games, eighty-two starts.
A brute that loves to battle. It challenges anything that comes near.
That's Draymond. Eight point two rebounds and three point seven assists a night.

beats.vo: It changes color to blend in with its surroundings, then strikes before anyone notices.
Zero starts all season, off our bench. Then he starts in the Finals, and wins Finals MVP.
That's a team we're taking into any gym in the league.

facts.claim: 3P% = three-point (3) field goal percentage, as listed by ESPN
Our starters in the title-clinching Game 6 of the 2015 Finals: Andre Iguodala, Harrison Barnes, Draymond Green, Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson
Curry: NBA Most Valuable Player 2015 (first of 2 MVPs, 2015 and 2016)
Thompson and Curry earned the nickname the Splash Brothers; 2015 champions
Iguodala: in 2014-15 a reserve for the first time in his career; captured the 2015 Finals MVP after returning to the starting lineup in the middle of the championship series
Lugia: so powerful even a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart houses
Squirtle: shoots water at prey; sprays foam from its mouth
Corviknight: the black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe
Crawdaunt: a brutish Pokemon that loves to battle; compelled to challenge other living things to battle
Kecleon: alters its body coloration to blend in with its surroundings, sneaking up on prey unnoticed
